idle_facts: Did you know the longest recorded chess game took 269 moves? It ended in a draw.
Stockfish evaluates millions of positions every single second on your phone.
The number of possible unique chess games is greater than the number of atoms in the observable universe.
The word 'Checkmate' comes from the Persian phrase 'Shah Mat', meaning 'the King is helpless'.
Deep Blue was the first computer to defeat a reigning world champion, Garry Kasparov, in 1997.
A knight can reach any square on the chessboard, but it always takes an odd number of moves to reach a different colored square.
The folding chessboard was invented by a priest who wanted to hide his chess set by making it look like two books.
Before the 15th century, the Queen could only move one square diagonally. Now she is the most powerful piece on the board.
The second book ever printed in the English language was about chess.
The shortest possible chess game is known as the Fool's Mate, taking only two moves.
In 1999, Garry Kasparov played a chess game over the internet against the 'World Team', consisting of over 50,000 people from 75 countries.
Chess was invented in India around the 6th century, originally known as Chaturanga.
During World War II, top chess players were recruited as codebreakers at Bletchley Park.
The mathematical calculation of absolute perfect chess play is known as solving chess, which is currently impossible due to the game's complexity.
If you put one grain of wheat on the first chess square, two on the second, four on the third, and keep doubling, you would need over 18 quintillion grains.
There are 400 different possible positions after just one move by each player.
There are 72,084 different possible positions after two moves by each player.
There are over 9 million different possible positions after three moves each.
The longest possible chess game without a capture or pawn move is 5,949 moves long.
Blindfold chess is a recognized variant where players do not see the board and must memorize the entire position.
Magnus Carlsen became a chess Grandmaster at the age of 13 years and 4 months.
The first modern chess tournament was held in London in 1851.
A pawn is the only piece that captures differently than it moves.
The rule of En Passant was introduced in the 15th century to balance the new rule allowing pawns to move two squares on their first turn.
Castling is the only move in chess where two pieces are moved in the same turn.
The physical design of standard chess pieces we use today is called the Staunton design, introduced in 1849.
A rook's original name was 'Rukh', which translates to chariot.
Chess is a required subject in schools in Armenia.
The FIDE rating system used to rank players was created by physicist Arpad Elo.
AlphaZero, an AI created by Google, learned to play chess from scratch and defeated Stockfish in just 4 hours of training.
During a single game of chess, players can burn hundreds of calories just through intense brain activity and stress.
The longest time a player has ever spent thinking about a single move in a professional tournament is 2 hours and 20 minutes.
Pawn promotion originally only allowed the pawn to become the piece it had replaced on that file.
Checkers is mathematically 'solved' and will always end in a draw with perfect play, but chess remains unsolved.
In 1992, a chess match was played in space between astronauts on the Soyuz spacecraft and crew on Earth.
Alice in Wonderland's sequel, 'Through the Looking-Glass', is heavily structured around a game of chess.
The term 'Grandmaster' was first used by Tsar Nicholas II of Russia in 1914.
It is theoretically possible to have nine queens of the same color on the board at the same time.
Chess clocks were first introduced in tournament play in 1883 to stop players from taking hours for a single move.
Wilhelm Steinitz was the first official World Chess Champion, claiming the title in 1886.
The 'Immortal Game' is a famous chess match from 1851 where White sacrificed a bishop, both rooks, and his queen to achieve checkmate.
In medieval times, chess was considered an essential skill for knights to learn.
The record for the most simultaneous chess games played by one person is 604.
Chess boxes traditionally have a green felt interior because green is soothing to the eyes after staring at the high-contrast board.
The youngest person to ever beat a Grandmaster in a standard tournament game was only 8 years old.
FIDE stands for 'Fédération Internationale des Échecs', the international governing body of chess.
Some early versions of chess featured dice to determine which piece you were allowed to move.
A 'stalemate' wasn't always a draw. In some eras and regions, the player causing the stalemate lost the game.
Bobby Fischer famously stopped playing competitive chess for 20 years after winning the World Championship in 1972.
Computer chess engines use an algorithm called Alpha-Beta pruning to discard bad moves quickly and calculate deeper.
